turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: Thanks for making the time today. I want to understand how your warehouse operates now, and where the biggest slowdowns are before we talk about any new system.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Our biggest pain is that inventory counts drift over the course of a week. By Friday the numbers in the system don't match what's on the shelves, and the pickers stop trusting them.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: That's useful. When the counts drift, what do the pickers do instead? Do they walk the aisle to verify, or do they escalate to a supervisor?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: They walk the aisle. It costs us maybe two hours a shift. We also can't promise same-day fulfilment because we never know if a bin is really stocked.

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: I'll add that our scanners are ten years old and only sync when they're docked. So any count taken mid-shift isn't visible to anyone until the device is back on the cradle.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: So if I'm hearing you both correctly, a constraint is that stock accuracy has to hold in real time, and an assumption we should validate is that same-day fulfilment depends on trustworthy live counts. Does that sound right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes, exactly. Real-time accuracy is the requirement. Same-day fulfilment is the outcome we care about, and it's currently at risk because of the sync delay Dev mentioned.
